proposals.title: Today's review: one spaced, interleaved, blind queue that never piles up
proposals.what:
A new first tab on /review/: `Today 12 · Redo 25 · Marked 3 · Saved 14 · History 312 · Fixed 40`. Each local day (X-Tz), the server builds a due list from five ladders, all on fresh seeds:
(a) first proofs: mistakes not answered since they opened;
(b) second proofs: mistakes whose first clean answer came on an earlier day (see proposal 2);
(c) check-ins on fixed mistakes (R9: 3, 10 and 30 days);
(d) saved questions on their own ladder of 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days, where a clean answer moves up a rung and a miss drops to rung 1 and opens a mistake;
(e) slow-right question types (proposal 5).

Size and order: the cap is 40% of the student's daily minutes (learners.minutes), at least 6 and at most 30 questions. Priority runs relapsed, then confident misses (proposal 4), then overdue, then due. The list is then interleaved so no two questions in a row share a topic. One slot in four is a 'cover' question of new material from progress.coach, so a redo question cannot be spotted as one. No card says 'your mistake' until after Check.

Card at the top of the tab:
- a ring `0 / 12` and the chips `5 first tries · 3 second tries · 2 check-ins · 2 saved`,
- `about 16 min` and the primary **Start today's review**,
- a 7-day forecast strip with a bar and count per day, today highlighted,
- the rule line: 'Each mistake comes back on new numbers until you get it right on two different days.'

When finished: `Done for today · 9 of 12 right · 2 mistakes fixed · 7 due tomorrow`, with the ring full. Unanswered items roll to the top of tomorrow. Anything over the cap waits and is never shown as debt. The nav badge becomes 'due today', not total open. Today's Review card and Plan's Rechecks task read the same list.

What the student does differently: one 15-minute review every day, instead of now and then clearing a 25-row backlog in one sitting. Why it moves the score: spaced retrieval on new numbers, mixed across topics, is the most reliable gain in learning research (spread-out practice beats practice crammed into one sitting, and mixing topics trains choosing the method). Cover questions remove the 'this is the arc one' cue that the real test never gives. A finite daily goal is what keeps a habit going.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has a 'Due Today' list only for vocab words. Their math redo list is always empty (toggleRedo has no button, and Profile reads 'Redo Questions 0'), and 'Solved Only' repeats the same finite items. Our v2 spec spaces only fixed mistakes; the rest is a backlog cleared with 'Redo all · 22'.

proposals.title: Proof that sticks: a mistake closes only on two different days, never right after reading its label
proposals.what:
This changes what closes a trap (R8/R9).
- **Pip 1** can be earned any time, including on the repair question straight after the miss (Repaired).
- **Pip 2** counts only when both hold:
  - it comes on a later local day than pip 1 (traps.proved_at, X-Tz calendar day);
  - it was not answered in the Review pane within 10 minutes of the student viewing that trap's label or rationale. Pane answers of that kind file attempts.primed = 1, fill no second pip, and show 'Practice. The proof comes tomorrow.'

Pip states: ○○ Open → ●○ `Back tomorrow · Sep 24` → ●● Fixed → check-ins at 3, 10 and 30 days (R9).

Other changes:
- drill._pick skips a trap whose proved_at is today.
- The Redo queue asks each template at most once a day, so the header reads `Redo all · 11 questions · about 18 min`, not 22.
- Session feedback copy (S4): 'Right: 1 of 2. It comes back tomorrow on new numbers.'
- The Fixed stat line adds `proved over a median 2 days`.
- Migration: traps closed today stay closed, and their first check-in is due tomorrow.

What the student does differently: they can no longer 'fix' a mistake in five minutes by spotting the trap they just read about. They have to recall the method after some forgetting has set in. Why it moves the score: success in the same session right after feedback measures short-term memory. A right answer after a delay is what predicts test-day performance. It also keeps Fixed honest, so the list reflects what the student will actually get right in March.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Mixed' is wrong-then-right on the same item seconds apart, with unlimited retries. The v2 spec lets a trap close within one session: the repair counts as a clean answer, and practice's _pick asks the topic's open trap again within 3 or 4 questions. In the seeded dev database, all 10 closed traps closed within 30 minutes of opening.
proposals.needs:

- R9's wording amended.
- counts.redo_questions becomes Σ open templates × 1 per day.
- drill._pick change (F5 → S4) and the S4 feedback copy.
- One test_flow assert: two right answers on one day leave owed = 1.

proposals.title: Name your own mistake before we name it, plus an inbox for test misses
proposals.what:
Every new miss enters Redo as `New · not reviewed` (an ink dot). That includes misses from sections, modules and the diagnostic, where no feedback was shown during the test. The tab head reads `6 new misses to look at · about 4 min`, with **Look at new misses**, which steps through them in the pane.

For each miss:
1. The pane shows the question with the student's pick marked and the key hidden.
2. It asks **What happened?** with 4 to 6 choices, shuffled and shown as plain sentences:
   - the misconception behind their pick,
   - the misconceptions behind the item's other wrong options,
   - 'Misread what was asked', 'Arithmetic slip / rushed' and 'Didn't know how to start'.
3. After the tap, the pane reveals the key and the per-option lines, with a verdict: `You called it`, or `Your pick came from: used 180 degrees for a whole circle`.
4. Then **Fresh one like this** (practice only; see proposal 2) and **Next miss**.

Keys: 1–6 to choose, Enter to reveal. The Redo head and the calibration panel show 'You named your own mistake 11 of 17 times (65%)', also per topic. The self-tags that are not misconceptions become Redo filters: Rushed feeds proposal 5, and Didn't know how to start sends the trap to the worked-example step of proposal 6. Grid-ins use spr_mistakes when the template has them (R9), and otherwise only the three general choices.

What the student does differently: they diagnose each error in about 15 seconds instead of glancing at a label, and test misses stop dying unread in a report. Why it moves the score: studies of self-explanation and of studying wrong worked examples (e.g. McLaren et al.) show that students who analyse their errors outperform, on delayed tests, students who were only shown the correction. Being able to name a trap is what lets a student catch it mid-solve on test day.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis' is passive prose inside one explanation. Their report cannot be re-answered, and their QBank hides the key after a miss. The v2 pane shows the label at once and gives the student nothing to do.
proposals.needs:
- A diagnoses(learner, attempt_id, choice, ok, at) table (F4) and traps.reviewed.
- POST /api/review/diagnose {attempt_id, choice}, which returns the reveal payload through access() 'reveal' (R19).
- A diagnose step in UI.review mode 'pane' (F3).
- spr_mistakes from the QBank bank task.
- A test_flow assert that the key is not returned before the diagnosis is posted.

proposals.title: Confident misses first: calibration across every sitting
proposals.what:
Every answer gets a confidence level:
- 'guess': practice's I'm guessing, or the Tests Guess tag;
- 'unsure': flagged, or the Unsure tag;
- 'sure': the Sure tag, or unflagged and within pace. The inferred case is shown as `sure (assumed)`.

Redo changes:
- Rows get a confidence glyph.
- **Confident misses first** becomes the default sort.
- A stat tile reads `CONFIDENT MISSES 4 · you didn't know you didn't know`.
- A confident miss carries a `Sure ✕` chip until it is fixed, and leads Today's review.

The Marked tab's calibration line becomes a panel:
- a 3×2 grid (Sure / Unsure / Guess × Right / Wrong) with counts and percentages;
- a table per topic;
- rules generated from thresholds: sure-accuracy under 80% in a topic gives 'Linear functions: 5 sure-but-wrong. Check your work here before moving on.' Unsure-accuracy over 70% gives 'Circles: you're right 78% of the time you doubt yourself. Trust your first answer.'

What the student does differently: they work first on the errors they would never have flagged on test day, and learn topic by topic when to trust themselves and when to re-check. Why it moves the score: the hypercorrection effect (Butterfield & Metcalfe) means high-confidence errors, once corrected, are remembered better than low-confidence ones. Unflagged errors never get a second look in Bluebook, so they are pure point loss. A calibrated student spends the last minutes of a module on the right questions.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep counts flags (the red For Review flag, the orange dot) and never relates them to correctness. The v2 spec's calibration is one ratio over flags only, and Tests' calibration is per sitting inside one report.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.guess and attempts.flagged (R8).
- attempts.conf, filled from qstate.conf (R7, S5) and from an optional Sure / Unsure chip in the practice session (S4, behind a pref).
- GET /api/review/calibration → {grid, topics, rules}, computed in SQL.

proposals.title: Slow but right: the pace list and speed-up sets
proposals.what:
A new Redo kind, `Slow` (clock glyph), computed from data. A template is slow when the student's last 2 right answers on it were both over its tier target, or over twice the student's own median. The tier targets are easy 65s, medium 95s and hard 125s, which gives about 2,090s for a 7/8/7 module against its 2,100s (R34). A row reads `Area of a sector · right 3× · median 2:40 · target 1:35`. Wrong answers given in under 25s get a `Rushed` chip and the rule 'Slow down on these: 4 misses in under 25 s'.

**Speed up** (action bar and pane) builds fresh versions with a target bar on the question strip: it fills orange until the target, then ink, with no hard cutoff. A right answer under target fills a pip, and 2 pips on different days (proposal 2) clear the item.

The History modal and the pane's family strip gain a time sparkline per try with the target line, e.g. `2:40 → 1:52 → 1:21`. A tile reads `SLOW RIGHT 6 · about 9 min over pace per module`.

What the student does differently: they drill the question types that eat their clock, against a visible target, until those types are fast as well as right. Why it moves the score: every minute over pace on a timed module is a question at the end that is rushed, guessed or never reached. Speed on routine types frees time and working memory for the hard ones, and today's mastery bars count slow-right as simply right, which hides the loss.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has a per-question stopwatch that resets on reload and is never analysed; nothing in their product talks about pace. The v2 Review only offers a 'Slowest' sort on History.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.ms in every mode (R7).
- PACE = {easy: 65, medium: 95, hard: 125} in blueprint.py, and one function progress.slow(learner) that Plan's slow-skill rule (S7) also reads.
- Trap kind 'slow' with norm '~slow' (F4).
- Drill cfg target_ms, rendered on the runner strip (F3, S4).

proposals.title: Stuck mistakes get a faded ladder: worked, then hinted, then solo
proposals.what:
A trap missed 3 or more times, or relapsed, gets the status `Stuck`, and its redo becomes a ladder. Each step uses a fresh seed:
1. **Worked.** The question is shown with the key highlighted, the rationale and every option's misconception. The task is 'Tap the option that comes from your mistake', then 'Got it'.
2. **Hinted.** A fresh version with a 'Watch for: used 180 degrees for a whole circle' line above the stem. A right answer fills a hollow step, not a pip, and is filed as attempts.scaffold = 1, which is neither clean nor counted toward mastery.
3. **Solo.** An ordinary fresh question inside Today's review, where a right answer is pip 1.

A miss at any step goes back one step. The pane shows the three steps with the current one ringed. 'Didn't know how to start' from proposal 3 also starts a trap at step 1.

What the student does differently: they stop hammering a question type they keep failing. Instead they study one worked instance, answer one with a hint, then go solo. Why it moves the score: worked-example and fading research (Sweller; Renkl & Atkinson) shows that learners who keep failing gain more from studying worked examples first, and that fading from worked to independent beats problem solving alone. Repeated failure with no new information only repeats the error.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep offers only unlimited retries on the same item, or reading its one explanation. The v2 spec serves another fresh seed of the same trap forever, however many times it is missed.
proposals.needs:
- attempts.scaffold INTEGER, excluded from clean answers and mastery (F4, extends R8).
- traps.stage, 0 to 3.
- Drill cfg scaffold: 'worked' | 'hint' (F5), rendered by UI.workspace (F3).
- Step 1 reuses the Spot-the-trap walk (POST /api/review/spot).

proposals.title: Habits: the handful of mistakes behind dozens of rows
proposals.what:
Redo's Group by gains **Habit** (`Topic | Domain | Mistake type | Habit`). A panel on the Redo head reads, for example: 'Your top habits: Reported the wrong quantity · 9 misses in 6 topics; Halved or doubled · 5 in 3 topics; Sign flip · 4 in 3 topics'.

There are about 10 habits: the wrong quantity asked for, sign, reciprocal or inverse, square vs root, half or double (radius vs diameter included), percent base, added vs multiplied, units, stopped one step early, off by one.

Each habit card has:
- a strip of its misses over time and the topics they came from,
- a one-line test-day check, e.g. 'Before you pick: underline what the question asks for',
- **Drill this habit**: an interleaved set of fresh items across its templates whose options include one of its traps (list 'related', generalised from a norm to a habit).

The mapping lives in server/habits.py: regex rules over the norm, with a bank-side Mis.habit tag overriding them where set. I measured it: over 12 seeds per template there are 2,524 distinct normalised reasons. Crude rules already match 1,187 of them (47%), and 'wrong quantity' alone covers 559 norms across all 19 topics.

What the student does differently: they fix one root habit with one self-check that works in every topic, instead of working through 25 separate labels. Why it moves the score: the same error pattern recurs across topics, and a named general check transfers. Mixing topics trains recognising the habit in a new setting, which is what the SAT demands.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep names no misconceptions at all. The v2 spec's 'same mistake elsewhere' matches only identical normalised text (79 norms), which misses most patterns that cross topics.
proposals.needs:
- server/habits.py: the rules plus an lru_cached index built like progress.related.
- Optional Mis.habit in satbank/item.py (bank owner; this extends the open Mis.tag question).
- Drill pool 'related' accepting {habit} (F5).
- The habit copy is owned here.

proposals.title: Worth most first: rank mistakes by how often they appear on the test
proposals.what:
A new sort, **Worth most**, which is the default on Redo. It ranks by expected questions lost: how often the topic appears on the test, times the student's miss rate on that template's last 5 answers, weighted by tier.
- Topic frequency comes from blueprint: the published 15/15/7/7 domain split per 44 questions, divided among topics by skill counts.
- Group headers show `≈ 4 questions a test`; row meta shows `costs ≈ 0.6 questions a test`.
- The Most-missed strip becomes `Worth most: these 5 cost about 2.4 questions a test → Redo these 5`.
- An optional points line, `≈ +20 points at your level`, uses the slope of the student's current estimate (R16). It is hidden when the estimate's confidence is low.

What the student does differently: with limited time, they fix first the mistakes the real test asks about most. Why it moves the score: a trap in Linear functions (about 4 questions a test) costs more than one in Probability (about 1). Ordering by test frequency times miss rate gives the most points per minute of review.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's redo list has no order, and it is empty. The v2 Most-missed strip ranks by hit count, which favours whatever the student happened to practise most.
proposals.needs:
- A TOPIC_SHARE constant in blueprint.py.
- The miss rate from attempts.
- estimate.py's slope for the optional points line (R16).
- sort=worth on GET /api/review/redo.

proposals.what:

What the student does differently: they write one line for each mistake they fix, and reread their own 20-odd rules the night before the test. Why it moves the score: the generation effect means explanations a student produces are remembered better than ones they read. A short personal list is the most useful final review there is, and no generic cheat sheet can match it.

proposals.title: Grade a paper worksheet in 30 seconds, so offline work counts
proposals.what:
The printable worksheet (§16) carries a short code and a QR on each page. Its answer page, `/review/print/?w=CODE`, has one row per number: A–D buttons, or a grid-in field with the usual keystroke filter, plus an optional 'minutes spent' box.

Mistakes are named and opened, and pips fill, exactly as online. The worksheet footer says 'Grade it at …/w/CODE' instead of 'These answers are not filed'.

What the student does differently: they do a worksheet on the bus or in study hall and get the same named-mistake feedback and credit as online. Why it moves the score: more retrieval practice without a screen, and none of it is lost. Today the spec's worksheet uses up seeds and files nothing, so a miss on paper never reaches Redo.

proposals.title: Review in 10 minutes: one ranked, time-boxed queue as the page's main button
proposals.what: The /review/ header's main button changes from 'Redo all · 22 questions · about 35 min' to a split pill **Start review · 10 min**, with a duration control `5 · 10 · 20 · All` above it. The choice is stored as a new pref, `review_minutes`, default 10. Under the pill, a live line says what the queue holds, e.g. `3 check-ins · 4 quick wins · 5 most-missed · closes up to 7 mistakes`. Tapping that line opens a UI.sheet with the exact queue, one row per question type (label, pips, why it was chosen). Each row has an X to drop it, and the sheet has Start at the bottom. The server builds the queue in `progress.review_queue(learner, minutes)`, in this order: (1) check-ins due, oldest first; (2) relapsed traps; (3) half-fixed traps, where owed = 1 and one clean answer closes each ('quick wins'); (4) blind spots (proposal 2); (5) open traps by points at stake (proposal 3), then by hits; (6) saved items due (proposal 9). The number of questions is floor(minutes*60/95), using the R34 pace. Each template is served at most once per round. Start sends `POST /api/drill {pool:'queue', minutes, source:'review'}`. The end screen reads `Closed 4 · half fixed 2 · relapsed 1 · open 25 → 21`, with **Another 10 min** and **Back to Review**. Today's #mist card (R30) uses the same pill. On /review/, the key R starts it. On a phone, the pill is full width with the duration control above it. When nothing is due, the line reads `Nothing due. 10 min of your most-missed instead`.
proposals.beats: It beats TopTierPrep's Redo List (All/Redo Only). Nothing ever fills their redo list: toggleRedo has no button, and Profile reads 'Redo Questions 0'. Their closest route is the QBank builder: open Advanced Filter, set Solved to Solved Only, then Start. That takes 4 steps and returns right and wrong answers alike, on the same numbers, in no useful order. Ours is 1 tap from Today or Review. It fits the time the student has, it is ordered by what closes mistakes fastest, and it says in advance how many mistakes the session can close.

proposals.title: Blind spots: find the answers you were sure of but got wrong, across every sitting
proposals.what:
At the top of the Marked tab, a **Confidence** panel. It has three parts.

(a) A 2×2 grid over every answer in the date filter. Rows are Sure / Unsure, where Unsure means the answer was flagged, marked guess=1, or tagged Unsure or Guess in a test. Columns are Right / Wrong. Each cell shows a count and a %, and a click opens History with that filter (`?confidence=sure&result=wrong`). The headline reads `Blind spots 14: wrong with no flag or guess` and `Lucky 5: unsure but right`.

(b) **Answer changes** across every test, from qstate.first against the final answer: `12 changes · 7 wrong→right · 3 right→wrong · 2 wrong→wrong · net +4`. The tip depends on the sign: net > 0 'Your second looks pay; keep flagging and returning', net < 0 'Your first answer is usually better; change only with a new reason'.

(c) **Flags you came back to**, from qstate.trail: `18 flagged · 11 revisited · 7 never revisited (4 of them wrong)`.

In Redo, a trap whose latest miss was not flagged, not a guess and not tagged Unsure gets a `Blind spot` chip. Redo also gains the sort `Blind spots first` and the Kind filter value Blind spot, and the queue in proposal 1 ranks blind spots above other open mistakes. For such a trap, the pane header adds `You were sure`.

Server: `GET /api/review/calibration?since=&until=` returns {matrix:{sure_right, sure_wrong, unsure_right, unsure_wrong}, changes:{n, wr, rw, ww}, flags:{n, revisited, never, never_wrong}}, computed in SQL from attempts (flagged, guess), flags and sessions.qstate. /api/review/redo items gain `blind: bool`.
proposals.beats: It beats TopTierPrep's report 'Flagged (n)' filter and their Mark for Review. They only count flags per report. They store no confidence, overwrite changed answers, and never connect a flag to its result or to a return visit. The Report section (S6) shows calibration for one sitting; Review adds it up over every test and every practice answer, then turns it into a priority. A sure-and-wrong answer is the mistake a student will not recheck on test day.

proposals.title: Mistake profile: the habits behind your mistakes, across topics
proposals.what:
Two new views:
- a **Profile** card above the Redo list, shown once the student has 10 or more misses;
- `Group by: Habit` in Redo.

The card has horizontal bars for these habit families:
- Answered a different quantity (solved for the other unknown, gave the whole instead of the remaining part, stopped a step early),
- Swapped the operation (added instead of multiplied),
- Sign slip,
- Flipped a ratio or reciprocal,
- Wrong percent base,
- Powers and roots,
- Units and conversions,
- Misremembered a formula,
- Counting and off-by-one,
- Arithmetic slip (the filler),
- Grid-in.

Each bar shows the family's share of misses in the last 60 days, its count, and an arrow against the 60 days before. Under it is one line of advice, written once per family. For example, 'Answered a different quantity: before choosing, reread the last sentence of the question.' Each bar has **Drill this habit · 8**. That builds fresh items across all topics whose options include a misconception from the family, walking at most 40 seeds per template.

Tag data, measured today: 386 templates give 2,271 distinct normalised reasons. A keyword pass classifies about half of them: answered-a-different-quantity 478, powers and roots 152, operation swap 145, sign 144, reciprocal or swap 120, percent 118, counting 76, units 67. The rest are tagged once in `satbank/habits.json` (norm → family) and reviewed by the bank owner. `satbank check` fails when a norm has no family. The server adds `progress.habit(norm)`. Me §3.7 'What keeps catching you' can show the top habit too.
proposals.beats: It beats TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis', which is prose inside one explanation, per question, and never added up. They cannot know that a student keeps solving for the wrong quantity in circles, systems and percentages. The spec's 'same mistake elsewhere' covers exact matches only (79 recurring norms); habits cover all 2,271 and find the test-taking habit that loses points in every topic.

proposals.title: 'Fresh one like this' shows the numbers changing, not a new question
proposals.what: In the pane (and the session's repair question), 'Fresh one like this' (key T) does not clear the question and redraw it. The stem stays in place, and only the tokens that differ between the old and new stem (numbers, variable letters, names) change: old fades to new in 220 ms with an amber underline that stays for 1.2 s. Figures cross-fade, and the choices re-render. For a student's first 3 uses, a caption reads `Same question type, new numbers`. Implementation: split both stems on /(\d[\d.,/]*|\s+)/, diff them with LCS (stems are at most about 400 characters), and wrap changed tokens in <mark class=chg>. The walk is a drill with cfg.inline and cfg.walk, and its position is kept on the server, so a reload or another device resumes at the same step. End card: '6 reviewed · 4 proven on new numbers · 2 still open · check-ins from Sep 26', then [Walk the 2 still open] and [Done]. proposals.title: Points at stake: every open mistake priced in SAT points
proposals.what: The server adds progress.stake(learner) and returns stake_pts on every redo item and group, plus a total. The estimate per trap multiplies four factors. (a) Expected slots per 44-question section: the domain's count from blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT (15/15/7/7), divided by the topics in that domain, times the template's share of its topic. (b) Exposure: the share of the template's seeds whose options contain the norm, from the related index (§14). (c) Fall rate: (hits+1)/(template attempts × exposure + 2). (d) Points per raw question at the student's estimate: the difference in the scoring curve at the raw score ±1 around estimate.mean3, or 500 with a 'rough' tag when there is no estimate. Values are rounded to 5 and capped per topic at slots × slope × (1 − accuracy). UI: each Redo row shows DM Mono '+10 pts' on the right; the header meta reads 'Open mistakes cost about 40–60 points a section'; the default sort is 'Points at stake'; the most-missed strip becomes 'Worth the most: Redo these 5 · about +30 pts'; the stat strip gets an AT STAKE tile. A 'How this is worked out' disclosure on the open row reads 'shows up in ~1.1 of 44 questions · you fall for it 2 of 3 times · each question is worth ~10 points at 560'. The Fixed tab gains 'Recovered ≈ +30 pts this month', taken from each trap's stake when it closed. The number is hidden until the student has 30 answers or a scored sitting.
proposals.beats: None of TopTierPrep's lists are ordered by value: their Redo filter is empty and unranked, and their domain cards give a confusing percentage. Pricing a mistake needs a labelled misconception, how often that option appears (only known because we generate the options), and the student's own fall rate across seeds. A student sees which ten minutes of redo are worth the most points.
proposals.needs: estimate.py mean3 (F4, R16), the scoring curve (scoring._interpolate), blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT, the related index (§14), attempts.norm (R8). No new column: exposure comes from the cached index, not from regenerating each attempt.

proposals.title: Trap gauntlet: sets where every question carries one of your own misconceptions
proposals.what: 'Trap gauntlet · 12' sits on the Redo header, on Today's Review card, and as a Source in the Practice builder. For each of the learner's open and check-due norms, the server takes the templates where that norm appears (the related index) and walks fresh seeds, at most 40 each (about 10 ms), until the four options contain the norm. It interleaves them so that no two in a row share a topic. It mixes in 20% control questions containing none of the student's traps, so a student cannot learn that 'the trap is always there'. Options: length 10/20, the clock off or at test pace (95 s a question), feedback instant or at the end. Nothing during play shows which option is the trap. Summary: 'You met 14 of your traps · dodged 11 · fell for 3', then one row per trap met (✓ dodged / ✕ fell, with the question number to open). A dodge on the trap's own template is an ordinary clean answer and fills a pip. A dodge on another template counts toward 'Dodged in 3 question types', shown on the Redo row and in the pane's Same-mistake-elsewhere line.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Redo and Marked filters can only re-serve items the student has already seen, and their distractors carry no labels, so they cannot choose questions by which wrong options they contain. This is 'drills built from a student's own misconception profile', testing transfer across question types, and it never runs out.
proposals.needs: The related index (§14); drill list 'related' extended from one norm to a set of norms plus control items (F5, R10); attempts.norm (R8); the session summary shows traps met and dodged (S4). The same seed walk as Spot the trap.

proposals.title: Why you missed it: an automatic cause per miss, confirmed in one tap
proposals.what: progress.record gives every wrong answer a cause, stored in attempts.cause with traps.cause_src 'auto'|'you'. The rules: a filler option means Slip; flagged or 'I'm guessing' means Unsure; ms below max(20 s, 35% of this learner's median on the template) means Rushed; otherwise it is Concept (the named misconception). The pane and the guided review ask 'Was this your mistake? <label>' with [Yes, that's it] and [No, I…]. No opens radio rows: Misread the question · Arithmetic slip · Guessed · Ran out of time · the item's other labelled misconceptions · Something else (80 characters). Slip, Rushed and Misread need 1 clean answer to close; Concept needs 2. The Redo header shows a 'Why you lose points' stacked bar with a legend and counts ('Concept 14 · Rushed 5 · Slip 4 · Misread 2 · Unsure 2'). Each segment filters the list, and each has a remedy button. Concept → Redo. Rushed → 'Slow-down set': fresh versions where Check unlocks after 30 s under a 'Re-read what is asked' line. Slip → 'Check-your-work set': after picking, a one-line estimate prompt comes before Check. Misread → a set where the question sentence of the stem is shown and tapped first. Unsure → Worked twin (proposal 6). Every 'No' is counted per (template, norm), and /admin/reports lists labels disputed by at least 15% of 20 or more learners.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis' is prose, and with unlimited retries they cannot tell which pick came first, so they cannot separate a concept error from a slip or a rushed read. Our labelled options, the filler tag, the time per answer and the flags make the cause computable, and the student's confirmation also tells us which labels in the bank are wrong.
proposals.needs: attempts.cause and traps.cause_src (F4, §2.5); guess and flagged (R8); ms on all attempts (R7); drill cfg modes 'slow', 'estimate' and 'misread' (F5, S4); the label-dispute view in the reports admin (F6, R17).

proposals.title: Instinct report: what your flags, first answers and blind spots are worth
proposals.what: A card at the top of Marked, plus an INSTINCT tile on the stat strip, covering the last 30 days. Block 1 is a flag matrix, 2×2 with counts, each cell a button that filters History or Redo: Flagged & right ('could have moved on'), Flagged & wrong ('good catch'), Not flagged & wrong, labelled **Blind spots** ('you didn't know you didn't know'), and Not flagged & right. Block 2 is answer changes, from qstate.trail in tests and from selection changes before Check in practice: 'Changed 17 answers: right→wrong 9 · wrong→right 4 · wrong→wrong 4. Your first answer was worth +5 questions ≈ +40 pts', with a split per topic. Block 3 is flag hit rate per topic: 'Your flags catch 30% of your Circles misses; flag more there.' Redo also gets a lens and sort, 'Blind spots first': wrong, not flagged, not guessed, and answered at or under the median time. It comes with [Drill my blind spots], which serves fresh versions at the tier of the miss. The spec's calibration line becomes Block 1's top sentence.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep counts flags and never says what they were worth. Their report overwrites answers, so they cannot know about second-guessing, and without time per answer they cannot find confident misses. This teaches the test-day skill of when to trust yourself, measured on the student's own data.
proposals.needs: The flags table (R5), qstate trail and changes (R7), selection-change logging in UI.workspace practice mode (F3), guess (R8), ms. Aggregates go on /api/review/marked (calibration becomes an object) and /api/review/redo?lens=blind.

proposals.title: Worked twin: 'See one solved' on new numbers, then 'Now you'
proposals.what: In the pane and in step 2 of the guided review, a button 'See one solved' sits beside 'Fresh one like this'. GET /api/review/worked?template=&tier= walks to an unseen seed that is not in today's challenge, marks it seen in practice_seen, and returns it with the answer, the rationale and the reasons. Nothing is filed, and History lists it as 'Viewed · worked'. At 1280 the pane shows two columns. Left: 'You missed', the original with your pick. Right: 'Worked · new numbers', with the key and rationale open, and the option carrying the same misconception as your pick outlined, labelled 'Same trap as your C: <label>. Here it gives 36.' Under both is [Now you: a new one], the inline fresh drill, so the order is example → attempt. On a phone the two stack, with a segmented You missed | Worked control.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep can only show the same item's explanation again, after which re-answering it tests memory. A worked example on different numbers followed by a fresh attempt needs an unlimited bank, and pointing at the same trap on new numbers needs labelled distractors.
proposals.needs: generate plus practice_seen (the worked seed is burned, so revealing its key is safe); deps.access to exclude the day's challenge (R19); UI.review pane (F3).

proposals.title: Speed repair: right answers that cost too much time
proposals.what: A 'Slow rights' lens on History and Redo selects right answers whose ms is over 2 × the 95 s pace, or over 1.5 × the crowd median for the template when n ≥ 20. Header: '18 slow rights in 30 days · about 21 min over pace'. The rows are grouped by template: 'Circles · Arc length · your median 2:40 · pace 1:35 · crowd 1:50'. [Speed repair] serves fresh versions of those templates. Each question shows a target clock, max(pace, 80% of your median), as a draining bar. Beating it twice in a row lowers the target by 15 s, down to the pace. A template is 'Up to speed' after 2 right answers on pace, which shows as a status in the Fixed tab. A wrong answer is filed normally and opens a trap; an over-target right is filed as right, with 'over target' in History.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows a stopwatch that resets on reload and never uses it. A speed drill on a finite bank turns into memorising answers, while fresh numbers keep it about technique. On the SAT, a right answer that takes 3 minutes costs points on the questions after it.
proposals.needs: ms on every attempt, tests included (R7, R8); the crowd median from drill.levels (the QBank section); a per-question target clock in the runner shell (F3, S4); drill cfg 'speed' with a per-template target (F5).

proposals.title: Paper that counts: printed worksheets whose answers still get filed
proposals.what: Print worksheet (§16) gains a 6-character sheet code, stored as a sets row of kind 'paper' with its items (R18). The printed header carries 'Check your answers at satfreshman/p/ABC234'. The options: Answer key on the last page (on/off; off for self-testing and tutors), Versions A / B (two seed sets on the same templates, for students sitting side by side), and 1–3 per mistake. /p/CODE shows a bubble grid, A–D per number or a grid-in field, with an optional 'Minutes taken'. Submitting files each answer through a drill with source 'paper'. Because the seeds are unseen they are clean attempts, so traps open or close, each miss is named, and a summary shows. A code can be checked once per learner, and a tutor who prints for a class has each student enter under their own code. This answers the open question on worksheet seeds: the seeds are consumed, and the answers are filed when entered.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no printables, and a finite bank would print the same pages every time. Paper practice normally never reaches the study record; here it does, with the misconception named for every wrong bubble.
proposals.needs: The sets table (F6, R18); the worksheet endpoint (§16); drill list 'share' or 'items' with source 'paper' (F5); deps.access (R19); print CSS.

proposals.title: My trap sheet and the exam-week pack
proposals.what: /review/sheet/ is one printable page, and a phone view, of the student's top 8 misconceptions by points at stake (or by hits before there is an estimate). Each entry has the label, the fix in one line (the first sentence of a fresh example's rationale), a tiny fresh example (the stem, then 'trap: 48 · key: 24'), the student's record ('dodged 4 of the last 5') and the topic glyph. Header: 'Read this before your test · Sat, Oct 3'. From 7 days before learners.exam_date, Today and Review show an 'Exam week' card with [Your trap sheet] and [Final check: one fresh question per trap · 8 questions · 12 min], the last one timed at test pace. The sheet regenerates its examples on every visit.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no personal summary of mistakes, and generic cheat sheets are not about the student's own errors. This is the student's own misconception profile on one page, with never-seen examples, for the morning of the test.
proposals.needs: Points at stake (proposal 2) or hits; generate plus the related index; exam_date (R15); print CSS; a hook on Today's #mist card (S3).

proposals.title: Evidence timeline: the life of each mistake, every step openable
proposals.what: For a trap, the pane gains a 'Proof' timeline built from the attempts rows with its template and norm, plus the trap's fields. Example: 'Sep 12 · Section #7 · Q14 · picked C = 48 · Wrong (Concept)' → 'Sep 12 · Repair · 24 ✓ new numbers' → 'Sep 14 · Practice · ✓ clean · Fixed' → 'Sep 17 · Check-in 1 ✓' → 'Sep 24 · Check-in 2 due'. Each node uses UI.resultCell and opens that exact (template, seed) in the pane, and Back returns to the timeline. A summary line reads 'Fixed in 2 days with 3 answers · held 10 days'. Fixed rows show the chain as a compact run of cells. Relapses appear as a graphite node ('Sep 30 · Relapsed · picked B').
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Attempt History covers one item in one session, and they never show that a mistake was fixed. A timeline that goes from the miss to proof on new numbers, and then to spaced checks, only exists because every question has an address and every miss a norm.
proposals.needs: /api/review/family with a trap filter (attempts by learner, template and norm); trap fields due, checks and relapses (R9); UI.resultCell (F1).

proposals.title: Proven-at ladder: difficulty that adapts per question type
proposals.what: Each trap carries rungs Easy · Medium · Hard, only those that drill._tiers_of has for its template. A rung is proven by a clean right at that tier after the trap opened. Fixed rows show 'Proven ▁✓ ▃✓ ▅○' with [Prove it at Hard] (one fresh Hard, inline). The Redo Level control gains 'Climb': start at the tier of the miss, step up after each clean right until Hard, step down after a miss (R33's rule applied per template). A trap that closed below the top rung is labelled 'Fixed at Medium', and its check-ins draw at the highest proven tier, so a check tests the level actually reached.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's redo has no link to difficulty, and their 1–7 score is only a filter. Here difficulty follows the student within one question type, which needs several tiers of the same template on fresh seeds.
proposals.needs: _tiers_of and attempts.difficulty; traps.proven (a small bitmask column, F4); drill level 'climb' (F5); R33.

parity_gaps.feature: Mark for review on the question strip (practice and exam runner)
parity_gaps.spec_says: A flag toggle (aria-pressed, orange when on) stored in the flags table per sitting, which survives a reload and module 2.

parity_gaps.upgrade: Let a flag carry a reason. A second tap on the flag, or Shift+M, gives three chips: Unsure · Guessed · Come back. The reason is stored in flags.why. Check your work lists 'Come back' first with its dwell time, the Marked tab groups by reason, and calibration works per reason ('your Unsure flags are right 70%: trust them more'). Setting or clearing a flag stays one tap.

parity_gaps.feature: The report's Flagged filter, corner flag and legend
parity_gaps.spec_says: Filters All · Wrong · Blank · Flagged (n), with a corner flag on cells and 'Flagged for review (n)' in the legend.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is TopTierPrep's All / R&W / Math / Flagged (n) with an orange dot, one to one.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Split flagged by outcome ('Flagged · 3 right · 2 wrong') and add a 'Blind spots (n)' filter: wrong, not flagged, fast. Add a 'Changed answers (n)' filter from qstate. Over the grid, one line: 'Your flags caught 2 of your 7 misses.'

parity_gaps.feature: Check your work FOR REVIEW card
parity_gaps.spec_says: The card reads the flags from the server.

parity_gaps.upgrade: Tie the card to the clock: '3 flagged · 6:10 left · about 2:00 each'. Order flagged questions by reason and dwell ('Come back' and the longest first). A cell tagged 'Guessed' gets a small ? so the student revisits the most likely flips first. This goes through the Tests owner (S5).

parity_gaps.feature: Difficulty filter and Details (TopTierPrep's Question Score 1–7)
parity_gaps.spec_says: The Review filters offer only Easy / Medium / Hard, and Details holds only the address and Copy link.

parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a Level chip to Review's filter bar using the QBank's measured levels ('measured from 42' or 'estimated'). The inline meta reads '▃ Medium · Level 5 · 41% of students right', and Redo's 'Harder' steps to the next measured level instead of only the next tier.

parity_gaps.feature: Question Overview views (Status | Difficulty)
parity_gaps.spec_says: The legend becomes Unanswered / Right / Wrong / Repaired / Flagged / Current, with a Status | Difficulty toggle.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: TopTierPrep has the same two views; Repaired is our name for their Mixed.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a Time view: cells shaded against the 1:35 pace, with the seconds printed. Add a Traps view: after answering, cells whose options contained one of the student's open misconceptions get a dot ('3 questions here had your traps; you dodged 2'). Both come from data only we have.

parity_gaps.feature: Saved content card on Me
parity_gaps.spec_says: 'Open mistakes 25 · Marked 3 · Saved 14 · Fixed 40 · Answers 312', each linking to its tab.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: TopTierPrep's Profile card shows the same kind of counts. Links are the only difference.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Show movement and value: '25 open (−4 this week) · 6 fixed this week · ≈ 50 pts at stake · 2 check-ins due', with [Redo the top 5] inline.

parity_gaps.feature: Share a set (§15)
parity_gaps.spec_says: POST /api/shares and a /s/ landing with Start (the exact items) or Fresh versions. Nothing about visitors is ever shown. (This conflicts with R18, which unifies shares into sets with /s/?c= and an owner-only results endpoint. R18 should win.)
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: TopTierPrep has shared sessions with a 'Start Practice' landing. Theirs freezes the page, but ours is the working version of the same feature.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Make it 'Challenge a friend'. With the opt-in show_score/show_name from R18, a visitor who finishes sees 'You 7/8 · Sam 5/8 on these questions' and which traps each person fell for. Add 'Fresh for each friend': every visitor gets their own seeds on the same templates, drawn so the same misconceptions appear among the options, so classmates cannot pass keys around. The sharer gets a results list with trap counts per question.

parity_gaps.feature: Eliminations and answer changes kept on the server
parity_gaps.spec_says: R7 stores struck options and the trail in qstate, but the Review pane shows only the pick and the key.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: TopTierPrep also saves eliminations and also never shows them in review.
parity_gaps.upgrade: The pane replays 'Your path': the options the student struck are drawn struck, with answer changes ('B → C at 1:10'), dwell time, and their highlights and notes (R6). The student sees when they had the right answer and changed away from it.

parity_gaps.feature: Prev / Next in the review view
parity_gaps.spec_says: Prev/Next through the current list with J/K and ←/→, and '3 of 25'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: TopTierPrep's review modal has ← → and '1 of 49'.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Mark rows already opened this visit with a seen marker, and add 'Next unreviewed'. When the list is sorted by points at stake, Next follows the value order, so pressing → always goes to the most valuable mistake not yet reviewed.

parity_gaps.feature: Wrong-number chips per sitting
parity_gaps.spec_says: History's sitting headers carry Again, exactly / Fresh versions / Fix the misses / Report, but no chips per question.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is below parity in scanning: TopTierPrep's cards list the wrong numbers ('2 3 4 5 6 7 +19'), even though theirs cannot be clicked.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put clickable result cells for each question in the sitting header. Each opens that question in the pane and shows the misconception on focus or hover. Add [Walk these misses], which starts the guided review.

parity_gaps.feature: Export (History CSV)
parity_gaps.spec_says: A Download CSV button on the History summary card.

parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a read-only Review page to the R18 progress link, for a tutor or parent: redo with stakes, the cause mix, the fixed log and the trap sheet. Add a printable 'Error log': for each mistake, the question, the pick, the named misconception, its one-line fix and its status.

parity_gaps.feature: Volume and Timed options when practising from a list
parity_gaps.spec_says: Only Redo's action bar has Level and Timed. Marked, Saved and History offer only Exactly / Fresh and 1–3 each.

parity_gaps.feature: Report a problem from the review view

parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a quiet 'This label is wrong' link beside each misconception line. It opens UI.report with the category 'Wrong mistake label' and (template, seed, option) filled in. It also takes the 'No' answers from 'Was this your mistake?', so the bank owner gets per-label dispute rates instead of free-text reports.

parity_gaps.feature: Empty state for a new student
parity_gaps.spec_says: A three-line panel (Redo / Marked / Saved, each explained), then Start practice and Take the diagnostic.

A wrong answer creates the first redo row live, with its named misconception and pips; a right one shows 'This is what a clean answer looks like' and offers a flag-and-answer to create an Unsure. The new student leaves with one real entry and knows how the page works.
